distinction: Previous whole-prefix certificate required even products nonzero while odd operands were unrestricted; it failed on real zeros. This hypothesis proves a different sufficient mathematical domain for BOTH products. It does not vary the old guard threshold, certificate granularity or numerical tolerance.
proof: Every operand is BF16 signed zero or absolute bits[0x2000,0x5f7f]. Nonzero products have <=16 significant bits, magnitudes >=2^-126 and <=(255/128)^2*2^126; thus exact finite normal FP32.
Original p=FMA_RN(a,b,+0), q=FMA_RN(c,d,+0). Nonzero products exact; zero products become positive zero. No odd negative-underflow zero is possible.

If ab nonzero, RN(p+q)=FMA_RN(a,b,q) since p is the exact real product. If ab zero, q is nonzero or positive zero; adding the signed product zero cannot change q, including q=+0. Opposite nonzero cancellation produces +0 in both expressions. Pair overflow also agrees.

Keep all higher pair merges, warp tree, scale and publication unchanged. Out-of-domain inputs require original arithmetic; a certificate must bind actual Q and K including speculative append, rollback/reset and causal lifetime.
validation: Authenticate all eight historical real captures; inspect ALL256 dimensions, not only even product dimensions. This remains necessary feasibility, not current MTP admission.

One native SM87 raw-bit comparison: all65536 BF16 codes as each of four operands against fixed directed signed-zero/exponent/mantissa corner triples; execute fast form only under complete predicate. Check out-of-domain controls and preserved original negative-zero counterexample.
If both pass, a separately bounded native certificate ownership/executor and current real API composition is required. No runtime retention or speedup is granted by arithmetic testing.
